# 0014 Reconstruct the engine as readable source

Status: in progress (generated layer done and reviewed 2026-10-15, fixes from the review pending, curation not started)

Owner's direction (2026-10-15): clean up the decompiled vendor code so that the owner, the orchestrator and subagents read and understand it faster. The code should look as if we had written it by hand: a proper file structure, not one function per file, and a high-level architecture that follows what the original authors intended. Caveat from the owner: if the decompiled code is heavily optimised or link-time optimised, the original architecture is hard to recover and the gaps have to be filled in. The decompiled output stays untracked (`CLAUDE.md`, "Sensitive data"), so everything here has to be regenerable from the scripts in `tools/ghidra/` plus tracked notes, and the hand-curated part needs a home that survives regeneration (see "Versioning" below).

Optimisation level, from the decompiled bodies: every parameter is spilled to a stack local at entry (`local_14 = param_1; local_10 = this;` in `CAsic::MotorSel`, `0x05d5f0`), the same getter is called again for each use instead of once (`CRegistry::MotorReg` three times in a row in the same function, `CRegistry::MotorPowerFBSel` three times per branch in `CAsic::MotorPowerSel`, `0x05e990`), the 278 one-line register accessors per class are out-of-line calls, and every method starts with its `LogToConsole(5, "Class.Method.IN")` string. That is unoptimised code with intact method boundaries, and the macOS binary keeps about 10,000 C++ symbols with demangled signatures (`doc/vendor-driver/macos.md`, "Symbols"). So the class structure, the call graph and the member layout are recoverable, and the gaps are the member names (offsets only) and the Windows engine's missing symbols, not the architecture *(inference from the samples read so far; the reconstruction step confirms it class by class)*.

What there is now (2026-10-15): `work/re/decomp-x86_64/` holds 2710 files for the macOS engine, one per function, flat, named `Class__Method@address.c`: 382 `CAsic`, 284 `CRegistry`, 278 each for `CGL846`, `CGL128`, `CGL126`, `CGL125` (the register accessor classes, mostly one-liners), 156 `CScan`, 140 `CIOUSB`, 110 `CScanApi`, 48 `CAfe`, the AFE chip classes (`CWM8199`, `CES8140`, `CHT82V36`, `CAD9826`), `CMap`, `CAddOn`, `CRegister`, `CNotify`, and about 60 libc, CoreFoundation and thunk entries. `work/re-win/decomp-x64/` holds 2184 files for the Windows V5.0.2.0 engine, 1818 of them `FUN_<address>` without symbols, 112 `Unwind` stubs. Next to them: disassembly, function tables, call lists, string lists, scalar scans and the accessor facts, flat in `work/re/` and `work/re-win/`. The Ghidra output has known readability problems (`tools/ghidra/README.md`, "Notes on reading the output"): `this` shown as a named parameter when the method is not marked `__thiscall`, small constants printed as Mach-O header fields, and the virtual base casts `this + *(long *)(*(long *)this + -0x28)` (the `CRegistry` subobject) and `-0x20` (the `CIOUSB` subobject) on every line that touches the registry or the bus.

Language and original layout, from the binaries (2026-10-15): C++, written Windows first. The classes carry the `C` prefix and `m_` members of Windows C++ of the 2000s, the macOS build shims Win32 names (`WaitForSingleObject` at `0x01d100`, `CKernelObject::ExCreateEvent` at `0x0811f0`, `CSecurityAttributes`), and the Windows engine carries "Microsoft Visual C++ Runtime Library" (`work/re-win/strings-x64-ascii.txt`). The macOS slice was built with Apple clang (`___clang_call_terminate`), uses no STL beyond `std::terminate`, and its symbol table keeps the build's object paths and source names (`work/re/strings-x86_64.txt` lines 5509 to 5513: `/Volumes/Macintosh HDD/GL12X/ScanApi-1.4.27.3.0/build/GL-126.build/Release/ScanApi.build/Objects-normal/x86_64/AD9826.o`, then `Sources/AD9826.cpp`, then `Includes/Register.h`). The source names embedded there give the authors' own file split: `Sources/Api.cpp`, `Asic.cpp`, `Afe.cpp`, `AddOn.cpp`, `AD9826.cpp`, `ES8140.cpp`, `HT82V36.cpp`, `WM8199.cpp`, `GL125.cpp`, `GL126.cpp`, `GL128.cpp`, `GL846.cpp`, `ConsoleDebugging.cpp`, `KernelObject.cpp`, `MacUtility.cpp`, `Map.cpp`, `Notify.cpp`, `Register.cpp`, `Registry.cpp`, `Scan.cpp`, `SecurityAttributes.cpp`, `USB.cpp`, with `Includes/*.h` for the classes, and Windows-era names `Scndll.cpp`, `Vxdif.cpp`, `MEM.cpp`, `MAPTOOLS.cpp`, `ScanApi_vers.c`. The symbol table's debugging entries map each function to its compile unit (checked 2026-10-15, `tools/ghidra/macho_source_map.py`, output `work/re/source-map-x86_64.tsv`, untracked): 2553 function start entries (`N_FUN`) in 27 compile units (`N_SO` with `N_OSO` object files). The `N_SOL` entries do not name each function's file, as first read: each sits inside the function that first uses a file and every file appears once in the whole map (corrected 2026-10-15, raw entry order dumped from the slice), so they give only the header names (`Includes/Asic.h` first used by `CAsic::_LPERIOD(bool, int)`, `Includes/notify.h` by `CNotify::EnableSuspend`). Inline definitions are told apart by the symbol table instead: 1716 functions are weak definitions with hidden visibility (inline, defined in a header), 816 strong external (the `.cpp`), 14 weak external (template instantiations), 7 local. Functions per unit: `Asic.cpp` 750, `Api.cpp` 499, `Scan.cpp` 397, `AddOn.cpp` 367, `USB.cpp` 134, `Afe.cpp` 110, `Map.cpp` 70, `Registry.cpp` 29, `Notify.cpp` 18, `MAPTOOLS.cpp` 17, `Register.cpp` 15, `Vxdif.cpp` 15, the four `GL*.cpp` 14 each, the four AFE chip files 10 to 13 each, `KernelObject.cpp` 9, `ConsoleDebugging.cpp` 7, `SecurityAttributes.cpp` 6, `Scndll.cpp` 5, `MEM.cpp` 4, `MacUtility.cpp` 2, `ScanApi_vers.c` 0. The Windows-era files live in a `FilmApi/` directory next to `Sources/` and `Includes/`. The reconstruction uses this map as the file split; only the Windows engine, which has no symbols, is matched by code.

Target shape (as built 2026-10-15, in the submodule `engine/`, see "Versioning"): a C++ source tree of the engine in the split the binary's debug map records, one `macos/Sources/<Unit>.cpp` per compile unit (`Api.cpp` holds the `CScanApi` methods next to the `api*` entry points, `USB.cpp` the `CIOUSB` methods, and so on), the four Windows-era units under `macos/FilmApi/`, one `macos/Includes/<Class>.h` per class with its declaration, the reconstructed virtual base helpers (`registry()`, `usb()`, `asic()`), the data members the code reveals and the class's inline definitions (the 1716 weak hidden definitions of the symbol table), `Sources/Unmapped.cpp` for the 156 functions without a debug map entry, and `notes/architecture.md` with the units, the entry points and per class its bases, virtual bases with slot and offset, own vtable and callees. Every function keeps `// at 0x<address>` with its demangled signature so that every document citation still resolves. The Windows engine comes second, as the same tree with the functions matched to the macOS ones (same code base, `doc/vendor-driver/windows.md`), unmatched functions left under their addresses.

Deliverables:
- [x] Ghidra pass, scripted and tracked in `tools/ghidra/` (2026-10-15): `macho_engine_tables.py` reads the class table, the vtables with every virtual base's slot and offset, and the 264 registry keys from the binary; `ApplyEngineTypes.java` runs on a fresh import (`work/ghidra-typed`) and applies `__thiscall` with the demangled parameter types to 2289 member functions, `bool` returns from the epilogue pattern, the class structures (a `vptr` into a vtable structure with a named field per virtual base, `CRegister::m_reg`, the GL classes' `regBuf` and `regShadow`, `CRegistry::m_prop` typed as the key table) and removes the `__TEXT` block at address 0 so that constants print; `DumpClassMembers.java` writes the members out. Re-decompiled into `work/re/decomp2-x86_64/`. The reviewer compared all 2403 class functions against `c++filt` (2375 exact), confirmed the disassembly at `0x033b43` for the corrected argument lists, and counted the artefacts before and after (Mach-O header constants 955 to 0, `CONCAT` 1219 to 40). Open: about 18 member functions with enum parameters keep Ghidra's own list, and 1009 keep an undefined return type (a committed `void` broke callers).
- [x] Reconstruction script `tools/ghidra/reconstruct_engine.py` with `test_reconstruct_engine.py` (2026-10-15): writes the tree above from the source map, the members and the decompiled directory, with the virtual base casts rewritten to helpers, virtual calls through bases named, spills folded only when the types are equal and neither side changes, dead locals dropped, and each `m_prop` read annotated with its plist key (all 250 accessor names equal their keys, so the annotations sit on the accessor bodies). The reviewer regenerated everything from scratch byte-identically and found the rewrites meaning preserving over the whole tree. Fixes pending from the review: the parser mishandles definition heads Ghidra wraps over several lines (54 methods declared `static` by mistake, 38 without a return type, 1210 call sites left in the `Class::Method(usb(), ...)` form), the dead-store regex matches lines that start with `Class::Method(`, the regenerate commands lack a `mkdir`, and the long functions of the three scripts.
- [ ] Curation by hand, class by class in order of relevance (`CAsic`, `CScanApi`, `CScan`, `CIOUSB`, `CRegistry`, `CGL126`, `CAfe`): member names from their use, local variable names, comments only where the code does not say it, the one-line verdicts already established in `doc/protocol/` and `doc/vendor-driver/` at the methods they concern. The curated text lives as patches or as the curated tree in the private versioning below, so that a regeneration does not lose it.
- [ ] Navigation notes, tracked in `doc/vendor-driver/engine/`: the architecture README's source of truth and the agent note, copied into the tree by the script. `tools/ghidra/README.md` updated to the new commands and layout, and the existing documents' citations (`doc/protocol/playbook.md`, `serial-flash.md`, `serial-eeprom.md`, `macos.md`, `windows.md`) brought to the new paths.
- [ ] Review by a second agent: regenerate from scratch with the documented commands, confirm the tree and the notes match, and read three methods cold to judge the reading speed and whether the architecture reads as intended. First pass done 2026-10-15 on the generated layer (byte-identical regeneration; `CAsic::MoveCarriage` reads like source, `CScanApi::Register` is followable but littered with dead stores and raw offsets, `CIOUSB::WriteRegs` is clear apart from its declaration; `notes/architecture.md` correct but thin, with purposes for 5 of 20 classes and no hierarchy overview). To repeat after the fixes and after the curation.

Versioning (decided by the owner, 2026-10-15): the reconstructed and curated source lives in the private GitHub repository `Tubbles/plustek-scanapi`, added here as the submodule `engine/` (`CLAUDE.md`, "Reconstructed engine source"). The owner intends to move it to a self-hosted git server later. The raw Ghidra output stays in the untracked `work/re/` and `work/re-win/`, regenerable, and the reconstruction script writes into `engine/`. So the target shape above is `engine/macos/Sources/`, `engine/macos/Includes/`, `engine/windows/` and `engine/notes/`.

Related: `0005-vendor-driver-analysis.md`, `0012-driver-playbook.md` (the consumer of this layout), the owner's decision that the output stays out of git (`doc/log/2026-10-15.md`).
